Jamal Khan: FYI — we just got a DSAR from an ex-employee asking for deletion of their chat history + embeddings. Legal flagged that this identity is tied to an ongoing vuln triage (VG-903) so they're asking for hold. They also want us to perform targeted forensics which requires temporary decrypt access to a key. What is the approved 'break‑glass' process for KMS access?

Priya Patel: If Legal is asking for a hold we need a documented retention exception. For break‑glass we usually grant an ephemeral role via PrivGate, TTL-limited, with signed justification + 2-person approval. Is this for decrypting backups or in-place keys?

Jamal Khan: Mainly in-place keys for extracting minimal logs and correlating user actions (not exporting full key material). We'll also need to purge embeddings later after hold is lifted.

Alex Chen: Short answer: we can't export raw key material (HSM), but we can grant decrypt-only session tokens tied to the keystore service account. Typical flow: create ephemeral session via PrivGate -> issue decrypt token scoped to key:read:decrypt -> all actions logged to audit and linked to a case id. Example command we use in infra runbooks:```/privgate grant --user jamal.k --role dsar-temp-decrypt --ttl 4h --case VG-903 --approvers "priya,alex"```Audit tag: case=VG-903, purpose=forensics, retention=365d (unless Legal requests more).

Samira (Legal): Confirming hold. Do NOT delete anything until vuln triage note cleared. For the DSAR we can produce a redacted evidence package, and after triage if no legal hold remains we will issue deletion token. Any access MUST have: (1) case id in logs, (2) attestation phrase signed by approvers, (3) copy of request stored in PrivGate record.

Jamal Khan: Thanks. Two clarifications: 1) who will own the RBAC change (creating dsar-temp-decrypt role)? 2) where do we put the audit retention exception ticket?

Priya Patel: I can own the RBAC change. I'll open an infra ticket to add a short-lived role template (dsar-temp-*) and a policy that enforces approvers and TTL. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1456 — I'll add checklist items for attestation and case tagging.

Alex Chen: I'll update keystore runbook to include the CLI snippet above and a reminder to set KV-cache purge=0 for any in‑memory session data before leaving. Also add an automated post-session scrub step to queue embeddings deletion (vectordb prune command) once hold is cleared. Example prune command:```vectordb prune --case VG-903 --owner jamal.k --confirm```.

OpsBot: [automated] audit_id=aud_20260318_0902 created for case=VG-903, session=privgate-789, approvers=[Priya Patel, Alex Chen]. Actions will be retained for 365 days unless legal extends.

Priya Patel: New RBAC workitem created and linked in the ticket. I'll coordinate with Alex on runbook changes. We should also add a short attestation template that approvers paste into PrivGate with the case id.

Samira (Legal): One more: redact PII in any logs we export. If logs need to be kept for forensics, Legal will request a retention exception and document scope. We prefer audited artifacts sent to secure legal bucket, not personal drives.

Jamal Khan: OK — plan: Priya owns RBAC, Alex owns runbook + vectordb prune, Samira owns retention exception + legal hold clear. I'll schedule a 15m sync in 30m to confirm actions. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Priya Patel: I'll post updates in the ticket and tag this thread when the role template is live.

Alex Chen: If anyone needs to test the flow, we can run a dry-run with a synthetic case id. Use case test VG-TEST-1.

Samira (Legal): Good idea — please keep dry-run logs separate and flagged test=true.

Jamal Khan: filing the sync calendar invite now.
